text: 🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

Fresh-cut stems on the southwest ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Emberhold's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

The southwest ground is thinning faster than your crews alone could strip it. Emberhold isn't slowing down — their foragers are on your turf most days now. Their speaker would probably want words. (Talk about the shared ground at their fire.)
A runner from Emberhold, dusty and direct: "Your foragers are stripping our side of the southwest ground. Back off — or we'll talk with teeth." (Trust -3. The commons cuts both ways.)
A voice behind your eyes — bright, delighted, utterly wrong. (The System has arrived.)
🦎 "Those were CALIBRATION fauna! First drafts! The audience has NOTES! So we made BETTER ones!" (Something new is crying in the treeline.)
